answer: An AI‑agent marketplace forces each new participant to post a signed “quill” proof that references a recent, unpredictable system state drawn from a cryptographic hash of the last block, then obliges the agent to embed that proof inside a randomly chosen “vine” of neighboring agents whose reputations are tied to a shared ledger. The network monitors the depth of each vine; a Sybil cluster must generate a full canyon‑length chain of distinct proofs, each requiring fresh computational work and stake deposits, before its answers are accepted as genuine.
